claimBoundary: This is one provenance-bound Codex pass. It is single-model evidence, not human, instructor, independent, classroom, or multi-judge validation.

claims: A while loop repeatedly runs its body as long as a loop condition stays true, re-checking the condition before each iteration.
After each pass through the body, the loop expression is evaluated again to decide whether to continue.
If the loop expression is true, the body runs again; if it is false, the loop terminates.
A loop whose condition never becomes false runs forever — an infinite loop — so the body must make progress toward ending the condition.
attribution: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §5.1 While loop

artifact.df: A loop that keeps running because its condition never turns false.
artifact.eg: A file-reading loop that never advances the file position can keep printing the same line forever.
artifact.mi: It is any loop that runs a lot of times.
artifact.cx: A loop can run many times and still end normally; it becomes infinite only when the stopping condition never changes.

artifact.df: A programming construct that repeats a block of code based on a specified criterion.
artifact.eg: Using a while loop to process user input until a specific command is entered.
artifact.mi: Thinking a loop only runs once per condition check.
artifact.cx: The construct repeatedly runs its body as long as a loop condition stays true, re-checking the condition before each iteration.

claims: A variable is a name that refers to a stored value; the assignment operator = binds the name on the left to the value produced on the right (for objects it binds the reference, so no copy is made).
A statement sets a variable to a value using the assignment operator (=), with the name on the left and the value on the right.
Assignment is not mathematical equality — = copies a value into a variable rather than asserting two sides are equal.
A variable name may contain letters, digits, and underscores and be any length, but cannot start with a digit.
Variable names are case-sensitive, so total and Total are two different variables.
attribution: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §1.3 Variables

artifact.df: Names that are treated as different when their letters use different capitalization.
artifact.eg: total and Total can refer to two different variables in a trace of a program.
artifact.mi: Changing only capitalization leaves the name unchanged.
artifact.cx: Python distinguishes total from Total, so the capitalization matters.

artifact.df: The symbol used to set a variable to a value using the assignment operator.
artifact.eg: The statement 'x = 10' uses the assignment operator to set the variable 'x' to the value 10.
artifact.mi: Thinking the operator checks for mathematical equality between the two sides.
artifact.cx: The assignment operator sets a variable to a value, and assignment is not mathematical equality; it copies a value rather than asserting two sides are equal.

claims: A function is a named, reusable block of code defined with def that runs only when it is called; variables created inside it are local to that call.
A function is defined with the def keyword, a name, parentheses, and a colon, with an indented body.
A variable's scope is the part of the program where it can be accessed.
A variable created inside a function has local scope and cannot be accessed outside the function.
A variable created outside any function has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program.
attribution: OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, §6.1 Defining functions; §6.3 Variable scope

artifact.q: A classmate wants to write a Python function that prints a result when called. Which definition matches Python's function syntax?
artifact.ex: Correct: a function is defined with def, a name, parentheses, and a colon, followed by an indented body. A plausible mistake is leaving out the parentheses and colon, but Python requires both in the definition line.

artifact.q: Where can a variable created outside any function be accessed?
op: Only within the function where it was defined.
Only in the immediate block following its creation.
Only in the function where it is first used.
artifact.ex: The correct choice is that a variable created outside any function has global scope and can be accessed anywhere in the program. The misconception is assuming that variables defined outside a function are restricted to the function where they were initially created.

claims: The rock cycle describes how Earth's three rock families — igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic — form and continually transform into one another through geologic processes.
The rock cycle describes the major Earth materials, the processes that form them, and how they relate to each other.
Igneous rock forms when liquid rock freezes solid; lithified sediment becomes sedimentary rock; pre-existing rock can transform into metamorphic rock.
If conditions melt the rocks into magma, the cycle begins anew with new igneous rocks.
attribution: An Introduction to Geology (opengeology.org), §4 The rock cycle

artifact.q: When liquid rock cools and solidifies, what type of rock is produced according to the cycle?
artifact.ex: Option C is correct because igneous rock forms when liquid rock freezes solid. Option A is incorrect as metamorphic rock forms from pre-existing rock under different conditions, and Option B is incorrect as sedimentary rock forms from lithified sediment.

artifact.q: After a rock melts, the geologic cycle can start over when the molten material cools and hardens. What new rock family forms first?
artifact.ex: Igneous rock is correct because liquid rock freezes solid to form igneous rock. A plausible misconception is to choose sedimentary rock, but sedimentary rock forms when sediment is lithified, not when magma cools.

claims: Geologic time spans the roughly 4.5-billion-year history of Earth; relative dating orders events by which is older or younger, while absolute dating assigns numerical ages in years.
Absolute (numerical) dating assigns specific ages in years to mineral grains within a rock.
By the principle of superposition, in an undisturbed sequence the bottom layers are oldest and the upper layers younger.
By original horizontality, sediments and lava flows are laid down horizontally, so tilted layers were disturbed after deposition.
The Earth is about 4.54 billion years old, and this vastness of geologic time allowed life to evolve.
attribution: An Introduction to Geology (opengeology.org), §7.1 Relative dating and geologic time

artifact.df: A way to place events in older-to-younger order rather than give a numerical age.
artifact.eg: A student decides which of two rock layers formed first in an outcrop.
artifact.mi: It always provides the exact number of years for a rock.
artifact.cx: Relative dating tells sequence; absolute dating gives numerical ages.

artifact.df: Assigning specific ages in years to mineral grains within a rock.
artifact.eg: Determining the exact age of a specific quartz grain in a sandstone sample.
artifact.mi: Assuming that relative dating methods can provide precise numerical ages.
artifact.cx: Absolute dating assigns specific ages in years to mineral grains within a rock.

claims: In music, a triad is a set of three notes (or "pitch classes") that can be stacked vertically in thirds.
A seventh chord is a chord consisting of a triad plus a note forming an interval of a seventh above the chord's root.
The seventh destabilized the triad, and allowed the composer to emphasize movement in a given direction.
There are four different inversions of a seventh chord.

artifact.df: A three-note sonority built by stacking notes in thirds.
artifact.eg: A student identifies C–E–G as a triad in a harmonic analysis.
artifact.mi: It must always contain four notes.
artifact.cx: A triad has three notes; adding a note a seventh above the root turns it into a seventh chord.

artifact.df: The vertical arrangement of notes that form a harmonic unit.
artifact.eg: A C major triad is C-E-G. A C dominant seventh chord adds a note to this structure.
artifact.mi: A chord is simply a collection of notes played simultaneously.
artifact.cx: A chord structure describes how notes are stacked vertically, which is the basis for understanding chord construction.

claims: In music, form refers to the structure of a musical composition or performance.
The term "binary form" is used to describe a musical piece with two sections that are about equal in length.
Musical form unfolds over time through the expansion and development of these ideas.
Form in music is the result of the interaction of the four structural elements described above [sound, harmony, melody, rhythm].
Subdivisions of each large musical unit are shown by lowercase letters (a, b, and so on).
The next level concerns the entire structure of any single self-contained musical piece or movement.

artifact.df: The overall structure of a musical composition or performance.
artifact.eg: A listener describes how a movement is organized from beginning to end.
artifact.mi: It means only the melody line.
artifact.cx: Form includes the full structure, not just one element like melody.

artifact.df: The overall arrangement of musical ideas within a piece.
artifact.mi: Thinking structure is the same as musical form.
artifact.cx: Musical form is the structure of a musical composition or performance.

claims: In music, a triad is a set of three notes (or "pitch classes") that can be stacked vertically in thirds.
A seventh chord is a chord consisting of a triad plus a note forming an interval of a seventh above the chord's root.
The seventh destabilized the triad, and allowed the composer to emphasize movement in a given direction.
There are four different inversions of a seventh chord.

artifact.df: The process of determining the specific notes that form a harmonic unit.
artifact.eg: Constructing a chord by stacking three notes in thirds.
artifact.mi: Simply naming the notes present in a chord.
artifact.cx: The specific arrangement of notes that defines a chord.

artifact.df: A group of three pitch classes arranged by stacking in thirds.
artifact.eg: In a simple C-E-G sonority, the notes form a triad.
artifact.mi: It is the same thing as a seventh chord.
artifact.cx: A seventh chord adds a note forming a seventh above the root, so it is not just a triad.

claims: Accessibility and usability evaluation combines standards-based conformance checks with observation of representative users completing realistic tasks.
WCAG organizes web accessibility around the principles perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust.
Evaluation with disabled and older users can find barriers that conformance evaluation alone does not reveal.
A usability test observes users attempting to use a product or service while thinking aloud.
A single disabled participant's experience should not be generalized to all people with disabilities.
sourceContext.license: W3C Document License and U.S. Government Work

artifact.q: A student is evaluating a checkout flow by combining standards checks with watching representative users complete realistic tasks. Which activity best matches that approach?
op: Run a WCAG review and a task-based usability test
Map the page hierarchy for a redesign
Compare two visual layouts without users
artifact.ex: Correct: a WCAG review plus a task-based usability test combines conformance checks with observation of users doing realistic tasks. Misconception: a survey or layout comparison can help, but it does not directly pair standards-based checking with observed task performance.

artifact.q: Which activity integrates standards-based conformance checks with observing representative users performing realistic tasks?
op: D) Combining conformance checks with observed user performance
artifact.ex: Option C is correct because it directly combines standards-based conformance checks with observation of representative users completing realistic tasks. Option D is less precise because it only mentions combining checks with performance, omitting the standards-based conformance aspect.

claims: Journey mapping represents an end-to-end experience from the user's perspective so a team can see connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities.
A journey map should start from research about the steps users actually take and the transactions involved.
An experience map should make struggle points and candidate improvement areas visible.
A map can reveal dead ends where the user cannot continue toward the larger goal.
Journey analysis should include gaps between online and offline parts of a service.

artifact.q: A team is mapping a student’s service experience so they can identify connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities. What should the map represent?
op: An end-to-end experience from the user’s perspective
A list of interface screens in the order built
A database of all support tickets by week
A summary of team roles and deadlines
artifact.ex: Correct: an end-to-end view from the user's perspective shows the connected steps and where the experience breaks down. A common misconception is to treat mapping as a build plan or backlog list, but that does not show the user's full journey.

artifact.q: What is the primary purpose of journey mapping?
op: To document the final product design.
To show connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities.
To list all possible user features.
artifact.ex: The correct choice, 'To show connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities,' is accurate because journey mapping represents an end-to-end experience so a team can see connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities.
